la:noun:Mavors.html:
Māvors, vortis, m.
from mah, magh, to cut; Gr. μάχη, μάχαιρα, and vor, root of vortere; i. e. the turner of the battle
, old and poetic name for Mars (q. v.), the god of war, etc.
Prop.: urbs Mavortis, i. e. Rome,; ; ; ; ; : Mavors pater,: genitor Mavors,: Iliae Mavortisque puer,i. e. Romulus,.—
Transf., war, battle: civili Mavorte, Aus Idyll. 4, 65.— Hence, Māvortius, a, um, adj., of or belonging to Mavors or Mars (poet.): moenia, i. e. Rome,: tellus,i. e. Thrace,: conjux,i. e. Venus,: proles,i. e. the Thebans,; cf.: seges Mavortia belli,the armed men that sprang up where the dragon's teeth were sown,.—As subst.: Māvortius, i, m., Meleager, son of Mavors, Ov M. 8, 437; cf. ; but of Mars, Petr. poët. 124, v. 261; .—Transf., of or belonging to war, warlike, martial: Amazon,: tela,: vulnera,.
